about: Twelve Rustacean misses and fixes, each replayed by scripts/idiomatic_rust.py. bad triggers its rule message, good is clean.

pairs.title: Name cases: const type and function

pairs.good_code: fn get_first(v: Option<i32>) -> i32 { match v { Some(n) => n, None => 0, } }
pairs.title: Option with match, never unwrap

pairs.bad_code:
use std::fs;
fn read_len(path: &str) -> Result<usize, std::io::Error> { let s = fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap(); Ok(s.len()) }
pairs.good_code:
use std::fs;
fn read_len(path: &str) -> Result<usize, std::io::Error> { let s = fs::read_to_string(path)?; Ok(s.len()) }
pairs.title: Result with question mark, never unwrap

pairs.bad_code: fn sum(v: &[i32]) -> i32 { let mut total = 0; for i in 0..v.len() { total += v[i]; } total }
pairs.title: Iterators over index loops

pairs.bad_code:
struct Server { host: String, }
impl Server { fn set_host(&mut self, h: String) { self.host = h; } }
pairs.good_code:
struct Server { host: String, }
impl Server { fn with_host(mut self, h: String) -> Self { self.host = h; self } fn build(self) -> Self { self } }
pairs.title: Builder with chained with steps

pairs.bad_code: fn greet(id: String) -> String { format!("hi {}", id) }
pairs.good_code:
struct UserId(String);
fn greet(id: UserId) -> String { format!("hi {}", id.0) }
pairs.title: Newtype over bare String id

pairs.bad_code:
struct Lock { name: String, }
impl Lock { fn cleanup(&self) { println!("{}", self.name); } }
pairs.good_code:
struct Lock { name: String, }
impl Drop for Lock { fn drop(&mut self) { println!("{}", self.name); } }
pairs.title: RAII Drop over manual cleanup

pairs.good_code:
trait Ext { fn extra(&self) -> usize; }
impl Ext for str { fn extra(&self) -> usize { self.len() + 1 } }
pairs.title: Extension trait plus blanket bound
Borrowed str over owned String ref

pairs.bad_code: fn label(name: String) -> String { let owned: String = name.clone(); format!("hi {}", owned) }
pairs.good_code:
use std::borrow::Cow;
fn label(name: Cow<'_, str>) -> String { format!("hi {}", name) }
pairs.title: Cow for maybe owned text

pairs.bad_code: fn main() { let v = vec![String::from("a")]; for item in v.clone() { println!("{}", item.clone()); } }
pairs.good_code: fn main() { let v = vec![String::from("a")]; for item in &v { println!("{}", &item); } }
pairs.title: Borrow in loops, never clone
No Deref poly, no singleton, tiny unsafe
